agent_notes: Per the reviewer's request, 15:1-6 is placed in the night (vision at 22:00, stars after) and 15:7ff in the next day's daylight, with the sleep at that day's sunset. The alternative reading is one afternoon with 15:5 as seen within the vision (15:1 'in the vision', Rashi/Midrash); I rejected it since the stars need night and the text of 15:12 and 15:17 stresses the later sunset. 'That day' (15:18) is then the day of the sunset covenant.

agent_notes: הַפְּגָרִים: Rashi and Radak disagree on what the 'carcasses' are (the halves, or the whole birds). The word 'peger' normally means a whole corpse. I did not choose between them and kept 'carcasses'. Sources not seen directly beyond the packet are not cited.
Ramban's list of the four exiles (Bereshit Rabbah 44) is cited as in the packet; I paraphrased it and did not invent further parallels.

The 'four hundred years' is grammatically loose: it can attach to 'sojourner', to 'serve and afflict', or to the whole sentence. Ramban (who reads the verse as transposed) and Radak (who counts from Isaac's birth) disagree with the plain reading that the 400 years were all in Egypt, and with each other. The literal layer keeps the Hebrew order so the ambiguity survives; the commentary does not decide the chronology. Exod 12:40 gives 430 years, which I have not used as a source.

STEPBible glosses אֹתָם as 'them' and ועבדום as 'they will serve them'. Radak notes that the verb carries a pronoun suffix where Hebrew usually takes the preposition ב (as Onkelos renders it 'serve among them'), and that the antecedent of the suffix is debated: Israel serving, or Egypt serving Israel. I glossed it 'and they will serve them' and kept the ambiguity in the literal layer; the dramatic layer takes the plain sense that Abram's offspring serve the host nation.

[system:sys.faith_reckoned_righteous] Defined here for 15:6. The subject of 'he reckoned it' is ambiguous in Hebrew; I take it as the LORD crediting Abram (the traditional reading), though some read Abram crediting the LORD.

[instance:inst.gen_15.furnace_passes] Typed as a theophany: furnace and torch are widely read as signs of the LORD's presence passing alone between the pieces. The text does not name the LORD as the one passing; this is an interpretation.

[instance:inst.gen_15.covenant_pieces] The animals preparation (15:9-11) and the passage of the furnace (15:17) are one ritual spread over two events; I recorded sys.covenant_cutting at the preparation and the theophany at the passage rather than duplicating.
[entity:group.oppressing_nation] Unnamed nation of 15:13-14 (later read as Egypt). Kept as an unnamed group, not identified with loc.egypt or group.egyptians, because the text does not name it.

[entity:loc.egypt] 15:18 'river of Egypt' (nahar Mitsrayim) is a boundary marker, mentioned with the existing loc.egypt as the nearest entity; its exact identity (Nile or Wadi el-Arish) is disputed and no separate entity is created.

[event_links:evt.gen_15.future_revealed] The edge for the LORD judging the oppressing nation (15:14) was removed as requested; group.oppressing_nation stays MENTIONED. The approved edge.gen_15.yhwh_foretells_exile is locked and kept unchanged, so the judgment is not added to its description.
[component:comp.abraham.offspring.1] Inferred from Abram's own words in 15:2-3; it stays open in this chapter because no later verse here ends it.
[component:comp.abraham.heir.2] 'He that shall come out of your own bowels' is read as a state with value SON_OF_OWN_BODY; the son is not yet named, so no target entity is possible.
